experiment: 1H and 15N TROSY CPMG relaxation dispersion at 500 and 800 MHz
construct_or_mutation: Thermotoga maritima CheA P4l (residues 346–540), C-terminal His6 tag, linker-containing P4 domain
other_conditions: ~1.5 mM U-[15N,2H], ILV 13CH3 sample; regime (authors): exchange is fast compared to the change in the chemical shift of the nuclei between the ground and excited states; related structures: 1B3Q (P3P4P5 crystal structure used for mapping); the dispersing residues (1H: 360, 390–398, 400, 401, 403, 439; 15N: 391–395, 517, 518) are in T. maritima P4 numbering
dynamics_type: us-ms conformational exchange in the P4 helix region and nearby residues, linker-dependent
timescale: kex = ~1250 ± 100 s-1 (single global two-state fit over all dispersing 1H and 15N residues; reduced χ2 = 1.2)
author_claim: The linker-containing P4l construct shows microsecond-to-millisecond exchange in residues in or near the middle helix of P4, fitted with one global two-state process.
anchor: indicating that there is conformational exchange on the microsecond to millisecond time scale in the protein.
locator: Results, p. 2 and Figure 2; conditions: Materials and Methods, Protein Preparation and CPMG Relaxation Dispersion Experiments
caveat_note: The data are from the T. maritima CheA catalytic domain P4l (residues 346–540), not the E. coli CheA entry sequence (residues 1–132, the P1 region), so this is homolog evidence for a different domain. The paper gives only residue numbers without one-letter types for the dispersing residues, so residues_author and residues_entry are left empty. The minor-state population could not be determined because exchange is fast. The exchange process is not tied to a structure of the excited state. The buffer pH is given inside the buffer field as written in the paper.

experiment: 1H and 15N CPMG relaxation dispersion of P4 lacking the linker, compared with P4l
construct_or_mutation: Thermotoga maritima CheA P4 (residues 356–540) without the P3–P4 linker, C-terminal His6 tag
other_conditions: Dispersion data are in Figures S6 and S7 (supporting information, not in the text); field strengths for P4 are not stated separately; the CPMG methods are given for the P4l sample; residues are in T. maritima numbering
author_claim: Removing the linker strongly damps the 1H and 15N dispersion seen in P4l, so the P3–P4 linker affects the dynamics of the P4 residues.
anchor: Thus, the P3–P4 linker affects the dynamics of the residues of the P4 domain.
locator: Results, p. 2; Figures S6 and S7; conditions: Materials and Methods
caveat_note: The profiles are described as significantly reduced, not absent. No exchange parameters for P4 are given in the main text, so exchange cannot be excluded outside the CPMG window. T. maritima P4 is a homolog of a different domain from the E. coli CheA entry sequence. The sample labeling for P4 is not stated separately. The buffer pH is given inside the buffer field as written in the paper.

experiment: 1H–15N TROSY-HSQC of P3P4 R354D mutant at 600 or 800 MHz
construct_or_mutation: Thermotoga maritima CheA P3P4 (residues 290–540) with R354D linker substitution, C-terminal His6 tag
other_conditions: Spectrum in Figure S8; related structures: 1B3Q (P3P4P5 crystal structure showing the Arg354–Asp392 salt bridge in one linker conformation); M355A showed small shift changes near the catalytic center (Figure S11); residues are in T. maritima numbering
dynamics_type: mutation-induced line broadening and missing peaks, possibly conformational heterogeneity
author_claim: Replacing Arg354 with Asp dramatically changes the dynamics of the same P4 resonances and some P3 resonances, giving missing peaks and line broadening, possibly through more coexisting states.
anchor: Thus, we suggest that breakage of the Arg354-Asp392 pair by mutation might give rise to more states that coexist in solution, resulting in the observed resonance broadening.
locator: Results, p. 3; Figure S8; conditions: Materials and Methods, NMR Spectroscopy and Protein Preparation
caveat_note: The broadening is qualitative and the process behind it is not identified. The authors only suggest more coexisting states. No exchange rate, population or CPMG analysis is given for the mutant. The protein is T. maritima P3P4, a homolog and different construct from the E. coli CheA entry sequence, and the paper lists R354 and D392 only in T. maritima numbering, so residues_entry is left empty. The E. coli R325D mutant was tested only in biochemical assays, not by NMR. The buffer pH is given inside the buffer field as written in the paper.
